title: finding(plugin-designer): `ObjectManager` draws a delete action on system objects and silently drops the click — objectui#8674's shape, one component over
body:
Surfaced while implementing objectui#8674 (dev seat, session `session_01UzHd6hDYatoDn17BuwKxnZ`). ⛔ Unassigned; grading and `domain:*` are triage's. ⛔ NOT fixed in that card's PR — it is a second component, and keeping it untouched is what let that PR measure an unchanged caller as its control.

## Measured, on `b775500af`

`packages/plugin-designer/src/ObjectManager.tsx`:

```ts
const handleDelete = useCallback(async (record: Record<string, unknown>) => {
  const obj = objects.find((o) => o.name === record.name);
  if (!obj || obj.isSystem) return;      // ← silent no-op, before the confirm dialog
  const confirmed = await confirmDialog.confirm(...);
  ...
}, [objects, onObjectsChange, confirmDialog, t]);
```

…and the affordance is wired at the GRID level, once for every row:

```tsx
onDelete={readOnly ? undefined : handleDelete}
```

System objects are on screen by default — `displayObjects` filters them out only when `showSystemObjects` is false, and this repo's own `ObjectManager.test.tsx` pins the default with a case named *should show system objects by default*. So the reachable state is a system-object row carrying a delete entry whose click produces no dialog, no toast and no console message.

This is objectui#8674 verbatim, in the sibling component: `readOnly` is honest (the callback is withheld, so no button is drawn), `isSystem` draws the button and swallows the click. The two states differ in the code and do not differ on screen.

## Why it is cheap now, and why it was still not done here

objectui#8674 added the mechanism this needs: `ObjectGrid` now takes `rowOperations?: (record) => { update?: boolean; delete?: boolean }`, a per-row narrowing of the grid-level `operations` vocabulary. The repair is the same three lines `FieldDesigner` got — resolve the object for the row and answer `{ delete: !!obj && !obj.isSystem }`.

It was deliberately left out of that PR for one measured reason: `ObjectManager` is one of the untouched `ObjectGrid` call sites that PR used as its byte-identical control (the rendered DOM of its grid, container plus every row's opened kebab, hashes identically before and after — 92191 bytes, sha256 `80f5438a…`). Fixing it in the same diff would have consumed the control.

## One hazard for whoever takes this

`packages/plugin-designer/src/__tests__/__mocks__/plugin-grid.tsx` — which `ObjectManager.test.tsx` installs — renders a delete button for every row whenever `onDelete` is wired, and knows nothing about `rowOperations`. It therefore reproduces this defect by construction and cannot see the fix: a pin written against the mock stays green either way. objectui#8674's own pin renders the REAL `ObjectGrid` for exactly this reason. Either teach the mock the prop or render the real grid, but do not assert a rendered affordance through that double as it stands.

## Scope of the duplicate search behind this filing

Bounded, and said so rather than implied: the 300 most recent rows of the repo-scoped REST issues list in **all** states (3 pages of 100) were read, of which 144 are issues and not pull requests, covering numbers **8919–9218**. Titles were scanned for `ObjectManager` / `object manager`, and for a system + object + delete/remove intersection — zero hits, with lit controls on the same rows (`designer` matched 2, `grid` matched 7). Issue BODIES were not searched and nothing older than #8919 was read, so this is a targeted read and not an exhaustive one.

## Related

objectui#8674 (the same defect in `FieldDesigner`, and the `rowOperations` prop this would use) · objectui#6044 (why `isSystem` identifies these rows correctly at all).
